name: White Rice (cooked)
notes: Staple grain in Indian cuisine. High GI (~70). Better portioned for diabetics. Parboiled or basmati have lower GI.

name: Brown Rice (cooked)
notes: Whole grain option with more fiber and micronutrients than white rice. Lower GI (~50). Good for diabetes management.

name: Whole Wheat Roti (chapati)
notes: One medium roti (~40g) has approximately 120 kcal. High fiber helps blood sugar control. Staple of Indian meals.

name: Toor Dal (cooked)
notes: Split pigeon peas. Excellent plant protein source. Rich in folate, iron, and fiber. Staple protein in Indian vegetarian diets.

name: Moong Dal (cooked)
notes: Mung beans dal — easy to digest, low GI, suitable for weight loss and diabetics. Often used in khichdi.

name: Chickpeas / Chana (cooked)
notes: High fiber and protein. Low GI (~28). Excellent for diabetes, heart health, and weight management. Used in chana masala, hummus.

name: Rajma / Kidney Beans (cooked)
notes: High protein legume popular in North Indian cuisine. Kidney beans are rich in potassium, iron, and folate.

name: Soy Chunks / Textured Soy Protein (dry)
notes: Exceptional plant-based protein source (52g/100g dry). Rehydrated soy chunks have ~120 kcal/100g, ~18g protein. Ideal for muscle gain on vegetarian diet.

name: Paneer (fresh Indian cottage cheese)
notes: High-protein, high-calcium dairy. Not suitable for lactose-intolerant individuals. Good for muscle gain. Use low-fat paneer for weight loss.

name: Curd / Plain Yogurt (full fat)
notes: Rich in calcium and probiotics for gut health. Lower fat versions (dahi from skimmed milk) available. Commonly eaten in Indian meals.

name: Cow Milk (whole)
notes: Excellent calcium and vitamin B12 source. Contains lactose — not suitable for lactose-intolerant individuals. One glass (250ml) provides ~380mg calcium.

name: Eggs (whole, boiled)
notes: One large egg (~50g): 78 kcal, 6g protein. Complete protein with all essential amino acids. Yolk contains fat-soluble vitamins.

name: Chicken Breast (grilled/boiled)
notes: Lean, high-quality protein. Excellent for muscle gain. Low fat when skin removed. One of the best protein sources per calorie.

name: Oats (rolled, dry)
notes: Cooked oats (~100g dry yields ~250g cooked): ~389 kcal dry or ~71 kcal per 100g cooked. Beta-glucan fiber lowers cholesterol. Low GI. Excellent for heart health and diabetes.

name: Banana (ripe)
notes: One medium banana (~120g): ~107 kcal. High potassium supports heart health. Natural energy food. Moderate GI (~51).

name: Apple (fresh)
notes: Low calorie, high fiber fruit. Pectin (soluble fiber) helps lower cholesterol. Low GI (~38). Good snack for weight loss.

name: Spinach (raw)
notes: Excellent iron source (though absorption is enhanced by vitamin C). Very high in folate, vitamin K, and A. Good for anemia prevention.

name: Tomato (raw)
notes: Rich in lycopene (antioxidant). Vitamin C boosts iron absorption. Very low calorie. Supports heart health.

name: Broccoli (raw)
notes: One of the most nutritious vegetables. High in vitamin C and K. Contains sulforaphane (cancer-protective compound). Low calorie.

name: Almonds (raw)
notes: 10 almonds (~14g): ~81 kcal. Rich in vitamin E, magnesium, calcium. Healthy unsaturated fats. Good snack but calorie-dense. Heart-healthy.

name: Walnuts (raw)
notes: Highest omega-3 among nuts. Anti-inflammatory. Good for brain and heart health. 5 walnuts (~20g): ~131 kcal.

name: Flaxseeds (ground)
notes: 1 tablespoon (~10g): ~53 kcal. Highest plant source of omega-3 (ALA). Very high in fiber. Good for constipation, heart health, and hormonal balance.

name: Sweet Potato (boiled)
notes: Excellent source of beta-carotene (vitamin A). Moderate GI (~63). Nutrient-dense carbohydrate alternative to regular potato.

name: Masoor Dal / Red Lentils (cooked)
notes: High protein and very high fiber. Excellent iron and folate source. Good for anemia prevention. Quick cooking time.

name: Orange (fresh)
notes: Excellent vitamin C source (1 orange meets RDI). Vitamin C enhances iron absorption from plant foods. Low GI (~40).

name: Poha (flattened rice, cooked)
notes: Light Indian breakfast. Easily digestible. Often fortified with iron. Commonly prepared with vegetables, mustard seeds, and curry leaves.

name: Idli (steamed rice cake)
notes: Fermented rice and urad dal. Low fat, easy to digest. One idli (~50g): ~66 kcal. Good breakfast option. Fermentation improves nutrient bioavailability.

name: Upma (semolina upma)
notes: Semolina-based South Indian breakfast. Add vegetables to increase fiber and nutrients. Light and filling.

name: Peanuts (roasted)
notes: High protein plant-based nut. Good magnesium source. Note: common allergen. One handful (~30g): ~170 kcal, 8g protein.
